## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — Health & Failure-Mode Assessment

**Data basis:** latest reading timestamped **2024-01-19** (≈2.7 years old — flag this to the budget reviewers; there is no newer sample in the stream).

### Health index
- **Health index: 72.4 — Condition: Good** (all 15 inputs present; no gaps).
- Oil-quality inputs supporting it: dielectric rigidity 55 kV (good), interfacial tension 45 mN/m (excellent), DBDS 19 ppm (moderate — corrosive-sulfur watch item), O₂ 5,850 / N₂ 27,850 ppm (normal), CO₂ 1,340 / CO 32 ppm (low CO).

### DGA fault classification (computed manually — the `interpret_dga` service returned "LLM unavailable" twice)
| Ratio | Value | IEC code |
|---|---|---|
| C₂H₂/C₂H₄ | 7 / 16,650 = 0.0004 | 0 |
| CH₄/H₂ | 7,400 / 2,850 = 2.60 | 2 |
| C₂H₄/C₂H₆ | 16,650 / 5,470 = 3.04 | 2 |

Code **0-2-2 → thermal fault, T2/T3 boundary (300–700 °C, borderline >700 °C)**. Ethylene-dominant, acetylene essentially nil → **no arcing**. Corroborated by WTI 80 °C / OTI 85 °C with oil-temperature alarm and trip flags set.

### Failure modes ranked by evidence support
1. **Thermal Fault — Core/Winding** — C₂H₄ is the dominant gas, CH₄/H₂ = 2.6 and C₂H₄/C₂H₆ ≈ 3 place the hot-spot in the T2/T3 range typical of metal hot-spots (circulating currents, bad joints); WTI/OTI alarms active.
2. **Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating** — same thermal gas family, but C₂H₄ >> C₂H₆/CH₄ implies temperatures above the <300 °C oil-only (T1) range, so it ranks below core/winding.
3. **Tap Changer Mechanical Wear** — a high-temperature thermal signature with negligible C₂H₂ is classic for OLTC contact coking/overheating, and open WO 1000051 (P1, WAPPR) already suspects it.
4. Cellulose Insulation Ageing — CO only 32 ppm; CO₂/CO ≈ 42 suggests paper is not heavily involved.
5. Oil Dielectric Degradation — dielectric strength and IFT are healthy; DBDS 19 ppm is the only minor flag.
6. Partial Discharge in Oil — H₂ is elevated, but CH₄/H₂ > 1 is the opposite of a PD pattern.
7. Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress — water content 0 ppm.
8. Low-Energy Arcing (Sparking) — C₂H₂ 7 ppm, ratio 0.0004.
9. High-Energy Arcing — not supported.

### Oil resampling interval
Condition = Good and the top-ranked mode is thermal (not arcing) → per your rule: **annually**.
Engineering caveat for the budget narrative: absolute concentrations (C₂H₄ 16,650 ppm, CH₄ 7,400 ppm, H₂ 2,850 ppm) are far above IEC 60599 typical limits and sit uneasily with a "Good" score. If you want a defensible position, at minimum take one fresh sample now to replace the 2024 baseline, and treat the annual cadence as the floor.

### Work order history (last year)
Only one WO exists for this asset: **1000051 — OLTC inspection** (PdM, priority 1, WAPPR, reported 2026-09-30). **No oil filtration or regeneration** was performed in the last year, so the gas-based ranking is not understated by oil treatment; no re-baseline is triggered on that ground.
